clusters.name: Resource management
clusters.what: One bounded context — a bookable resource with a type, a calendar, conflict detection, check-out and check-in, a deposit, and the staff skills that qualify someone to operate it.
clusters.why: **The single largest cluster, and the one the delivery plan puts at P3.** Rentals (7.6, fifteen rows, none served), lockers, cabanas, wheelchairs and strollers, instructor and equipment allocation, maintenance resource planning, session manifests and event resourcing all resolve to it. **7.6.15 says so in the client's own words** — *not currently covered in the proposed solution*. Serial-number tracking is the sharpest form: a specific stroller checked out to a named guest and back.

clusters.name: Reporting data sources
clusters.what: One enum extension, not seventy-five gaps.
clusters.why: **BL-053 appears against 75 rows and BL-143 against 40, and they are the same finding from two ends.** BL-053 says *the generic builder covers it but the data source does not exist*; BL-143 names exactly where coverage stops — `DataSource` has fourteen values and the matrix asks reports about stock counts, workstations, principals, loyalty, reviews, queue entries, conversations, consent, seating, devices, maintenance and messaging. **Every one of those already persists.** This is a source declaration exercise, and it collapses 115 row-citations into one settled-lane edit.

clusters.name: Something happens, someone is told
clusters.what: One notification and alerting mechanism, guest-facing and operational, internal and outbound.
clusters.why: **Four entries, ~80 row-citations, one absence.** The guest half (BL-052) and the operational half (BL-152) are the same missing thing seen from two sides, and BL-155's outbound webhooks are the same again pointed outside the platform. **Every condition is already computed** — `RegisteredDevice.status` reaches `error`, `ShiftCloseResult.requiresAcceptance` fires on variance, `QueueFeedHealth.isHealthy` goes false, `PromotionUsage.isBudgetExhausted` knows the money ran out. Six contracts detect their own trouble and none tells a person. Retry, priority and channel failover (BL-174) are properties of the same mechanism.

clusters.name: Waivers, consent capture and guest documents
clusters.what: A configurable form the platform can present, capture, version and retain — serving waivers, demographic capture and surveys alike.
clusters.why: **Three separately-raised gaps with one shape.** A waiver is a versioned document a guest signs; a data-capture form is a configurable set of fields; a survey is a form with a scale. All three need field configuration, conditional logic, a captured response bound to a subject, a retained version and an erasure path. **2.15.13 and 22.13.5 ask for the same versioning `white-label.Policy` already implements** — *a guest who consented to version 3 consented to version 3*. Waivers carry the legal exposure and 2.15.7's parental consent is a distinct act; capture carries the CF-69 reporting obligation.

clusters.name: Portfolio, household and organisation
clusters.what: An owner that is not the buyer — a family, a school, a corporate account — holding entitlements and money for named members.
clusters.why: **Eleven appearances across ten sections.** Section 5.5 specifies it fully: multiple portfolios per account, a primary holder assigning entitlements, transfer between linked portfolios, shared wallets with individual tracking, merging while preserving balances, and restrictions on transfer, spending and age. **The corporate half (BL-035) and the partner hierarchy (BL-075) are the same shape in different contracts** and should not be built twice. **Age and spend limits on a child's portfolio are child-safety controls, not preferences.**

clusters.name: Payments platform
clusters.what: A gateway abstraction with routing, a stored payment credential, and the four things that depend on the credential.
clusters.why: **Tokenisation is the keystone.** Recurring membership billing (BL-100), wallet auto-reload, one-click checkout and payment links (BL-072) all require a stored credential and none can be designed until it is decided — and it moves the PCI boundary, which is a compliance position. Terminal behaviour (BL-119), tender-by-channel (BL-115), issuer promotions (BL-113), presentment currency (BL-070) and cross-currency refund rate (BL-087) are all properties of the same layer. **The integration register has Stripe amber and NI Payment Gateway red — Network International being the dominant UAE acquirer.**

clusters.name: Marketing platform
clusters.what: Four modules the matrix asks for and `marketing-crm` does not hold — journeys, gamification, SEO and the authoring surface — plus attribution.
clusters.why: **Each is a module rather than a gap, and journeys are the one that blocks the others.** A journey is a graph of steps with branches and waits; `CampaignTrigger` fires one campaign from one event. Sixteen requirements at 22.3 depend on it, and it compounds CL-03 — a journey with no business events to branch on cannot start. **SEO is twelve requirements against nothing, with `CMS-013` a specified screen and zero operations**, and `ContentPage` has a slug with no canonical URL or redirect, so every URL change silently breaks inbound links.

clusters.name: Loyalty earn, spend and membership benefit
clusters.what: The loyalty engine is configured and nothing runs it.
clusters.why: **Better built than first assessed** — `LoyaltyProgramme` carries `earnRules`, `tiers`, `pointsExpireAfterMonths` and `pointsLiabilityAccountId`, so the rules exist and post to a liability account. **What is missing is narrow: nothing applies the earn rules on a completed order, and a guest cannot spend points.** Membership benefits as automatic entitlements rather than discounts (BL-037) sit on the same mechanism, as does the guest-facing membership view (BL-016).

clusters.name: Guest self-service and identity
clusters.what: A guest cannot identify themselves by any token, correct their own record, recover a locked account, or export their data.
clusters.why: **BL-012 is a legal right rather than a convenience** — 22.13.13 asks for rectification under PDPL and `updateGuestProfile` is staff-only. **The 18 August workshop decided the unified profile** — *a single, unified customer profile across ticketing, F&B and retail* — which is BL-064's six appearances answered by the client. DSAR erasure is built and the access half is not.

clusters.name: Versioning as one mechanism
clusters.what: Eight entities need version history and one contract already implements it well.
clusters.why: **`white-label` has the pattern** — `listConfigVersions`, `restoreConfigVersion`, `diffConfigVersion` with a `contentHash` and `scheduledFor`. Products, events, recipes, access policies, recognition rules, approval matrices, device configuration and media templates each ask for the same thing. **Recognition rules are the sharpest**: after a restatement the question is which rule was in force on the day. `seating` versions by convention — structural changes to a published map are refused, so clone, amend and publish.

clusters.name: Developer platform
clusters.what: Four separable questions behind one uncontracted domain, and the commercial one comes first.
clusters.why: **Documentation is nearly there** — ADR-0024 makes the contract the deliverable and 25 OpenAPI files are the schema documentation; what is missing is a portal. **A developer is not a partner** — `registerPartner` onboards a reseller with credit and commission, and outbound credentials (BL-080) exist nowhere. **Rate limiting has a screen and no operation.** If integrations are a handful of named partners, an event feed and issued credentials suffice; if TICVAI is sold as extensible, that is a product line.

clusters.name: Authorisation and platform security
clusters.what: Whether to replace a settled role-based model, plus four security controls that are absent regardless of the answer.
clusters.why: **About a third of 3.3 is already met** by `Grant` with scope inheritance — real-time evaluation, caching, offline evaluation, least privilege, temporary grants, audit. The ABAC question is whether the remaining two thirds justify replacing ADR-0002 and ADR-0018. **Four things do not depend on that answer**: no password policy or lockout (BL-144), no SoD enforcement beyond one guard (BL-147), no IP or device restriction (BL-146), and **no device authentication at all (BL-161)** — a reader on a gate holding an offline package of entitlements, on an unauthenticated channel.

clusters.name: Catalogue product model
clusters.what: Twelve primitives the product model does not carry, and they are why domain 1 scores 31%.
clusters.why: **`catalogue` is a spine contract with 53 operations and the highest gap rate of any spine domain.** Purchase eligibility (BL-027, six appearances) is the most cited; future-dated publication (BL-054) is CF-74's misfiled pricing calendar; person type (BL-093) blocks the child-versus-adult light at the gate. **These are small individually and they compound** — a product cannot be published on a date, restricted to a buyer, priced by weekday, or told who may hold it.

clusters.name: Media and ticket production
clusters.what: Nothing produces a ticket — no template, no stock, no recycling, no wallet pass.
clusters.why: **A venue changing its ticket artwork has no path that is not a code change.** Media stock is unmodelled (which ribbon is loaded, how much is left), media cannot be released and reassigned, and replacement does not blacklist the old code — **though F23 states that rule for contractor badges and not for guest media**, so a replaced wristband may still open a gate. Apple and Google Wallet is the fourth appearance.

clusters.name: Partner and channel
clusters.what: A partner is a flat account with no hierarchy, no channel manager, no ERP interface and no branding.
clusters.why: **CF-128 found the integration register was built from the Integrations sheet alone** and missed the OTAs by name — Viator, Klook, Headout, GetYourGuide — telephony, and Oracle. The commercial model for a reseller is covered; **a live channel-manager feed is not**, and 3.7.1 asks for bundles containing external supplier products. ERP invoicing (BL-077) is cited fourteen times.

clusters.name: Finance ledger completeness
clusters.what: Ten things missing from an otherwise excellent double-entry model.
clusters.why: **`finance` answers 219 requirements at 18–20% and three sections at zero.** What is absent is bounded and specific: a **suspense account** (BL-142, settled lane) is the control that turns an unmapped posting into a visible balance somebody clears rather than a silent imbalance; **two recognition schedules may both claim a product kind with nothing resolving precedence** (BL-141), which is a silent double-recognition; a **deposit** is a liability taken before fulfilment and `createReservation` takes no payment at all; and **tax invoices and credit memos are a UAE VAT obligation** with mandated format and gapless numbering that interacts with ADR-0013 and ADR-0014.

clusters.name: Device fleet management
clusters.what: The device model registers and monitors and does not deploy, retire or link to an asset.
clusters.why: **`tenancy` covers more of domain 16 than its name suggests** — twenty device kinds under ADR-0015, heartbeat reporting *paper low, drawer open, reader offline*, remote configuration through `DeviceBinding`. **Firmware records a version and nothing deploys one**, which is a site visit per device for the life of the contract. **A device is not an asset**, so a scanner sent for repair leaves the device list saying it is merely offline. And staff devices cannot register for push (BL-163), so CL-03's alerting has nowhere to deliver on the staff side.

clusters.name: Seat map completeness
clusters.what: Everything that is a seat is well built; the map holds nothing else.
clusters.why: **`seating` scores 10% across 112 rows** — blocks with reasons, holds with TTL, buffer and orphan rules, recommendation returning contiguous groups, two-phase import validated against real client files. **The map itself is only seats**: no standing zone, suite, stage, entry or exit. `layerMapping` names a `stageLayer`, **so the importer can read a stage and the model cannot hold one** — and 21.8.3's accessible route needs entries and exits to route between, which is an accessibility obligation.

clusters.name: F&B kitchen and outlet operations
clusters.what: Seven F&B gaps, five of them settled by the client on 18 August.
clusters.why: **The 18 August workshop decided most of this cluster** — course-wise firing with an elapsed timer that resets per course, the table status flow *Available → Ordered → Table Closed → Reserved* with *Cleaning* rejected, an optional deposit against the bill, production and batch management with planned-versus-actual-versus-yield, and *Change Server* on the table activity log. **`TableReservationStatus` does not match the agreed flow and needs reconciling.** Allergens (BL-127) are the safety one: substituting an ingredient changes the allergen set, and `fnb-menuPublished` already carries `allergensChanged`.

clusters.name: Compliance and regulatory obligations
clusters.what: Six obligations that are legal rather than functional.
clusters.why: **Cookie consent (BL-073) is normally bought rather than built** — CF-127 asks build, buy or drop, and 22.10.29's analytics injection cannot fire before consent. **A personal-data breach has its own regulator and clock under PDPL** and no home, while `maintenance.reportIncident` handles physical incidents well. **Face Tag versus Face Pass is a retention distinction** — a same-day tag deleted at close is a far easier posture to justify than an enduring enrolment. Accessibility (BL-065) is a closed artefact class with authored content unchecked.

clusters.name: Product and catalogue operations at scale
clusters.what: Bulk operations, dry runs and the operational verbs a catalogue of thousands needs.
clusters.why: **The package simulates in four places** — `dryRun` on performance cancellation, recognition, FX revaluation and period close, each an expensive irreversible act — **and a promotion is the same category**: `budgetCap` stops it after the money is spent and nothing estimates exposure beforehand (BL-114). Bulk upload and environment import (BL-057) is cited seventeen times. **Performance targets (BL-098) are one of three artefact classes still open**, and a latency budget stated late is one met by accident.

clusters.name: Queue and wayfinding
clusters.what: The queue is well built for one lane, and the venue has no map.
clusters.why: **`queue` answers 46 rows at 15%** with wait-time provenance — sensor, throughput or manual, with `isStale` — and closure that releases and notifies every waiting guest because *closing without notifying is not offered*. **A queue has one capacity, no type and no operating window**, so nine queue types become nine queue records. **The wayfinding map is cited by three contracts and exists in none** (BL-011, CF-123), which also blocks the accessible route, the vehicle locator and the live access-point map.
